newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on dollar lack.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on dollar lack.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weak across the board on Monday after a dull session in which dealers held on to dollars ahead of expected rate hikes at the primary Cetes auction, traders said.
"I see people acting very much on expectations ... they're hanging on to their dollars for the Cetes auction," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 1.2 centavos weaker, at 7.7410/7.7460 and 7.7350/7.7400 per dollar, respectively.
The same-day peso earlier closed 0.8 of a centavo weaker at 7.7200/7.7250 per dollar.
Traders said they estimated that a hike of 100 to 200 basis points on primary Cetes rates would be enough to maintain the peso in a trading range of between 7.70 and 7.75 per dollar.
"The peso may firm up over the coming days if (primary interest) rates are assigned at attractive enough levels," said a trader.

Traders said the market was also awaiting the outcome of inflation figures for the first half of October, which are due Thursday. This would be a guide as to how attractive Cetes rates would be in real terms.
"September saw a seasonal spike in inflation, but October should be better," said a trader.
Analysts expected consumer inflation to be between 0.65 and 0.75 percent for the first half of October.
